full_judgment: 7. On hearing submission of the learner Advocate and perusal of the case records, i appears from the plaint of the present suit that Adam Ali Howlader claimed ownership of .7 acres of land recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 59 in the names of two brothers Bashiram Mondal and Radhanath Mondal stating that on the death of Radhanath Mondals, the suit land devolve, on his brother Bashiram who also died leaving the only daughter in Shushila Bala Shikder, and the plaintiffs predecessor Adam Ali Howlader Purchased the suit land from the said Shushila bala Shikder by a registered Kobala dated 03.01.1970. But the suit land was shown to have been auction purchased by the, Government (Defendant-I) for arrear rents. The, Same plaintiff previously filed title suit no. 219 of 1972 challenging legality of the said auction sale and subsequent settlement to the defendant 4. The defendant 4 contested the suit on the assertion that he acquired interest in the sui land by taking settlement from the Government So, if the alleged auction sale is decided to be legal in the previous suit, the plaintiffs claim of title by purchase from the female heir of the S.A. recorded tenant does not stand. The question termination of prior tenancy right o the S.A. recorded tenants by the impugned auction is essentially a vital issue which is directly and sub sequentially in issue in both the suits filed by the same plaintiff against the same set of defendants in respect of the same land.
